audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gave Irelia rows 3 and 5 and 'Skill' on rows 0,1,2,4 in both layers, while every why on the page describes Sett winning those stages and the packet chart reads Sett for rows 1-5.
audit.why: Irelia's Emerald+ win rate here is 45.63% over 1212 games, and the mirror (sett__irelia) already set rows 0-5 to Sett with row 6 to Irelia. The two directions must not contradict.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-5 flipped to Sett in both layers as one atomic group with the ratings moved to match; row 6 stays Irelia, which whys[6], spikes[3] and the mirror all support.

audit.whatIsWrong: The spike text is vague about which cooldown gates the lane, and phases[5] claimed the Blade of the Ruined King timing simply wins the stage.
audit.why: Facebreaker is a 490-range pull on 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s and Haymaker is 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s with a shield attached; The Show Stopper is 120/100/80s. Those numbers, not a generic item timing, decide when Irelia may commit.
audit.corrected: Facebreaker's 13s at rank 3 written into phases[2] and phases[3]; phases[5] rewritten so the first-item stage is fought on Facebreaker's cooldown rather than assumed won.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both mid and late told the player to hold Defiant Dance (W) to 'tank'/'eat the true-damage release' of Haymaker. Defiant Dance reduces PHYSICAL damage only; Haymaker's centre is true damage, so the charge does nothing against it. Also the missing-interaction file flags that Haymaker's shield absorbs the burst window, and spikes[2] used 'Show Stopper' instead of Riot's 'The Show Stopper'.
audit.why: Irelia W text: 'She takes reduced physical damage during the charge.' Sett W text: 'punch an area, dealing true damage in the center and physical damage on the sides.' Standing dead-centre inside a charged W is the single worst thing Irelia can do here, and the page was recommending it.
audit.corrected: Both fields now say Defiant Dance cuts only physical damage and cannot eat the true-damage centre — sidestep to the cone's edge; the shield-absorbs-burst point is stated in the first-item spike wording; the ability name corrected to The Show Stopper (R).

audit.why: The most punishable cooldown really is Facebreaker (16s at rank 1, 10s at rank 5); the page already trades around it once the numbers were added.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Sett must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Facebreaker (E) lands at 3 and its 490 range yanks you mid-Bladesurge, so hold the wave near you and step back to bait the grab.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Haymaker's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Sett's window: his Q ranks make every punch heavier and Haymaker's shield eats your burst. Trade only while Facebreaker's 13s is down.

edits.before: Blade of the Ruined King is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Haymaker's cooldown.
edits.after: Blade of the Ruined King helps, but grit refills faster than your ramp — fight only on Facebreaker's cooldown.

edits.before: Both spike, but his Show Stopper (R) suppress-slam answers your engage — he can suplex you off your minions so you have no marked target to reset Bladesurge off, while you can still E-stun and wall his retreat with Vanguard's Edge.
edits.after: Both spike, but The Show Stopper (R) suppress-slam answers your engage on a 120s cooldown — he suplexes you off your minions so you have no marked target to reset Bladesurge off, while you can still E-stun and wall his retreat with Vanguard's Edge.

edits.before: This is Sett's window, not mine — through levels 4-6 his grit trades and stored Haymaker are heavier than my un-stacked DPS, and the damage reduction during his W channel eats the burst I'd normally punish him with. I trade strictly when his Facebreaker is on cooldown: E-stun in, Bladesurge a reset, hold my own Defiant Dance W to tank his Haymaker release, then leave before the grab is back. At 6 his Show Stopper suppress is the trap — if he suplexes me off my wave I lose every Bladesurge reset target and get chunked, so I keep my Vanguard's Edge wall to body-block his retreat or peel his dash, never to open a fight he can flip with R.
edits.after: This is Sett's window, not mine — through levels 4-6 his grit trades are heavier than my un-stacked DPS, and the shield on Haymaker absorbs the burst I'd normally punish him with. I trade strictly on Facebreaker's cooldown, 13s at rank 3: E-stun in, Bladesurge a reset, then leave before the grab is back. Defiant Dance only cuts physical damage, so it cannot tank Haymaker's true-damage centre — sidestep to the cone's edge instead. At 6 The Show Stopper is the trap: suplexed off my wave I lose every reset target, so I keep Vanguard's Edge to wall his retreat, never to open a fight he can flip with R.

edits.before: My patience pays off here. At two-plus items my stacked Ionian Fervor on-hit shreds his armor and MR the longer I stick, and near-permanent Bladesurge resets mean I out-DPS even a Sterak's-tanky Sett if I make the fight long instead of trading the opener he wants. I don't dump my W into his Haymaker wind-up for nothing — I time Defiant Dance to eat the true-damage release, then E-stun, chain resets off any marked minion, and let the ramp do the work. Sett doesn't scale like me, so if I survived his mid-game grit I'm the better sustained duelist once the fight goes past his first big Haymaker.
edits.after: My patience pays off here. At two-plus items my stacked Ionian Fervor on-hit shreds his armor and MR the longer I stick, and near-permanent Bladesurge resets mean I out-DPS even a Sterak's-tanky Sett if I make the fight long instead of trading the opener he wants. Defiant Dance cuts physical damage only, so it cannot eat Haymaker's true-damage centre — sidestep to the cone's edge, then E-stun, chain resets off any marked minion, and let the ramp do the work. Sett doesn't scale like me, so if I survived his mid-game grit I'm the better sustained duelist once his shield is spent.

edits.before: Bank grit into a max-charge Haymaker (W) — front cone is true damage — and cash it the instant your W damage-reduction channel ends
edits.after: Bank grit into a max-charge Haymaker (W) — the centre is true damage and the shield absorbs your burst — and cash it as you commit

notes: Point 4 correction is the important one: two fields told the player to hold Defiant Dance to tank Haymaker's release. Irelia's W reduces PHYSICAL damage during the charge and Haymaker's centre is TRUE damage, so the advice was actively harmful — corrected to sidestep the centre. Chart flipped to match the mirror (sett__irelia): rows 0-5 Sett, row 6 Irelia, proposed as paired full/content edits.
